 Eagles placed Dameon Pierce on injured reserve.
 Jaydon Blue was signed from their practice squad to the active roster in a corresponding move. Pierce went down with an injury on a kickoff return in the fourth quarter of Monday’s game. The team has not announced the exact injury yet, but Pierce will now miss a minimum of four games. Blue will back up a still-very-injured Saquon Barkley. Barkley returned from his hamstring injury in Week 7, only to suffer a back injury in the process. Blue has an outside chance at starting for the Eagles this week, making him worth a look on waivers. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 Dameon Pierce 
 PHI 
 Running Back 
 #39 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) was taken to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Week 7 against the Cowboys. 
 Pierce was injured on a kickoff return in the fourth quarter and was taken to the locker room almost immediately following the ailment. No word on the nature of the injury, but Pierce would appear to be on the wrong side of questionable to return considering there is less than six minutes remaining to play in the fourth quarter. Saquon Barkley was previously deemed questionable to return with a back injury, leaving Elijah Mitchell to fill in for the remainder of the game. Pierce rushed 14 times for 47 yards and a touchdown prior to departing, adding one yard on one reception. 
 Jaydon Blue 
 FA 
 Running Back 
 #30 
 Eagles waived RB Jaydon Blue. 
 They tacked on a waived/injured listing for Carson Steele, leaving the backfield with just Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce on the active roster. Blue did not officially get into a game with the Eagles after signing at the end of August. He’ll look to catch on elsewhere. 
 Dameon Pierce 
 PHI 
 Running Back 
 #39 
 Dameon Pierce rushed 12 times for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers. 
 With Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, and Will Shipley all hurt, and Carson Steele getting injured early in this game, Pierce took every single carry for the Eagles on Sunday. He also played on 61 of the team’s 64 snaps. However, that wasn’t able to amount to much on the ground with all of Philadelphia’s injuries. Pierce was also asked to pass block a lot, which means he only ran a route on 15 of the team’s 52 dropbacks. That’s going to limit his fantasy value, and he looks like a TD-dependent FLEX play while he remains the starter. The upside is that there doesn’t seem to be anybody coming for his job until Barkley (hamstring) returns. 
 Carson Steele 
 PHI 
 Running Back 
 #34 
 Carson Steele left Week 6 against the Panthers with a shoulder injury. 
 Steele caught a screen pass in the flats and lowered his head to try and run over the defender. He came up holding his shoulder and had to have the shoulder immobilized as he walked into the locker room with his pads off. It had the look of a dislocation, which would mean Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue are the only two healthy running backs for the Eagles. 
 Saquon Barkley 
 PHI 
 Running Back 
 #26 
 Eagles ruled out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Panthers. 
 It was pretty clear that this was where things were headed when Barkley was unable to practice on Wednesday and Thursday. We do not yet know Barkley’s official Friday practice participation level, but he was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue will likely split touches this week. 
 Saquon Barkley 
 PHI 
 Running Back 
 #26 
 Saquon Barkley (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday. 
 Barkley is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for his team’s Week 6 game against the Panthers, potentially leaving Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue to split touches. Hopefully, reports clarify whether Pierce would handle a sizable workload as the de facto starter. 
 Dameon Pierce 
 PHI 
 Running Back 
 #39 
 Dameon Pierce rushed 11 times for 14 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars. 
 Pierce “added” two catches for -2 yards. He took over as the Eagles’ lead back after Will Shipley went down with a foot injury in the first half. Carson Steele did not see the field for a single offensive snap. Pierce would presumably in line for a workhorse role in Week 6 if Shipley and Saquon Barkley are both out, but his efficiency today speaks for itself. This isn’t an offense capable of opening running lanes, nor is Pierce a back who can make a lot out of a little. Pierce is a low-priority waiver wire add for Week 6. 
 Will Shipley 
 PHI 
 Running Back 
 #28 
 Will Shipley (foot) will not return to the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jaguars. 
 Shipley suffered the foot injury in the second quarter and was initially listed as questionable to return. He will now miss the remainder of the contest. Dameon Pierce is the only other running back on the roster with a touch today. Carson Steele is also active. 
 Will Shipley 
 PHI 
 Running Back 
 #28 
 Will Shipley (foot) is questionable to return in Week 5 against the Jaguars. 
 Shipley got stuffed on a carry in the second quarter and was checked out by trainers after the play. He went to the locker room after a brief trip to the blue medical tent. Dameon Pierce will be the next man up if Shipley’s day is over. Carson Steele is the only other back on the roster. 
 Saquon Barkley 
 PHI 
 Running Back 
 #26 
 Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday. 
 Barkley will likely be listed as a non-participant on today’s official injury report. He is unlikely to play in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Aside from Barkley, the Eagles have RBs Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce on the active roster. Shipley will probably lead the backfield in touches this week, but it could be a messy workload split.

 Dalton Kincaid (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice. 
 Kincaid briefly left the Bills’ Week 6 game against the Raiders with this injury, though it was called a rib issue at the time. He returned to the contest in the fourth quarter. Buffalo then got a well-timed Week 7 bye. A limited session today is nothing out of the ordinary for Kincaid. We fully expect him to play in Week 8 against the Ravens. In what could be the best game environment of the week, Kincaid remains a solid TE1 option. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 Since the Texans are on bye in Week 8, Noel will not be eligible to return until Week 13 against the Steelers. It’s a tough break for Noel, whose involvement had begun trending upward. Hopefully, his injured reserve placement allows him to hit the ground running when he returns. Noel does not need to be held on benches.

 Roquan Smith (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
 Smith was one of several Ravens defenders to miss today’s session, though we’re expecting some of them to get back on the field later in the week. Smith has one interception, one forced fumble, and two sacks across seven games this year. We’re already expecting a shootout between the Ravens and Bills on Sunday, but Smith missing the contest would certainly increase the odds of fireworks on offense. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak
